panel: notebook: 'In real programs: csv, json, and safer saves'
what: Opening this notebook page makes the whole page scroll sideways at phone width: the notebook and footer become 498px wide on a 390px screen. The checker misses it because it never opens notebook pages.
evidence: With the page open, document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth = 498 (closed: 390). The csv_demo.py pre.code inside .page-body .pair has scrollWidth 612, and the .pair/.p elements extend to x=477. Every notebook crop is 483px wide: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-6-10/a10/w390-068-nb-after-p55-page.png. This is the 'ch10 csv notebook overflow' item from QA_REPORT, still open.
fix: In ext/py-ch10.css, change '.notebook .page-body .pair { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }' to also give the pair and its pre 'min-width:0' (e.g. '.notebook .page-body .pair, .notebook .page-body .pair > pre { min-width:0; }'). Better, add '.page-body { min-width:0 }' / '.notebook details { min-width:0 }' in the engine so any long code scrolls inside its box. Make the checker open every <details> once at 390 and re-measure overflow.

what: On phones the fill-in-the-blank code wraps so heavily that blanks end up alone on their own lines and statements break in the middle, so the code is hard to read and the blank's place in the line is unclear.
evidence: Rendered line counts at 390, against real lines: p8 15 lines drawn as 29, p14 28 as 49, p18 18 as 32, p34 10 as 21, p39 20 as 37. In p18 'if item ___ totals:' is split across three rows and '= ___' sits alone on a row: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-6-10/a10/w390-022-p18.png (also w390-011-p8.png, w390-037-p32.png). It is milder in ch6 (after p23 and p41), ch7 (after p14), ch8 (after p34) and ch9 (after p30 and p41).
fix: Engine (comic-widgets.css): at max-width 640px give '.fill-code' 'white-space: pre; overflow-x: auto' like code blocks, so each line keeps its shape and the box scrolls. Or keep wrapping but add a hanging indent ('padding-left: 2ch; text-indent: -2ch' on each line span) and keep the input and the text around it together with white-space:nowrap.

what: Parsons lines break in the middle of identifiers and strings on phones (e.g. 'line.strip().sp' / 'lit(",")', 'count_rec' / 'ipes("recipes.t' / 'xt"))'), which looks like different code to a beginner.
evidence: The engine rule '.parsons li code { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }' at <=640px: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-6-10/a10/w390-037-p32.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-6-10/a10/w390-058-p50.png
fix: In the engine, use 'overflow-wrap: break-word' and insert <wbr> after '.', ',', '(' and spaces when rendering parsons lines, so breaks land at punctuation. Or let parsons code scroll sideways ('white-space: pre; overflow-x:auto') like other code.

what: The tap-each-part anatomy line is cut off after 'with open("note.txt",' on phones. The "w", 'as f' and ':' parts sit off-screen in a sideways scroller with no hint, and at 1280 the line overflows its box by 9px.
evidence: p.anat-line scrollWidth 727 vs clientWidth 718 at 1280. At 390 it scrolls and the last parts can't be seen: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-6-10/a10/w390-026-p21.png
fix: Let the anatomy line wrap between parts at <=640px ('.anat-line { white-space: normal; }', keeping each .part 'white-space: nowrap'), or lower its font size with clamp() as ch8 p19 does.
